info.description:
The AerScheduler REST API. Schedule aircraft, close flights out, invoice them, and pull the numbers back , from your own software.

## Getting started

**The API is part of the Enterprise plan.** API keys can only be created, and only
work, for an organization on Enterprise. If **Settings → API keys** is not in your
console, that is why , talk to us at https://www.aerscheduler.com/contact and we will turn it on.

**The API is used with an API key**, and only with an API key.

Create one in the web console at **Settings → API keys**. Give it a name you'll
recognise and tick the roles it needs. The secret is shown once, at that moment,
and is never retrievable again , we store only a hash.

The roles a key may hold are `admin`, `dispatcher`, `instructor`, `student`,
`renter` and `technician`. `owner` cannot be granted to a key. Give a key the
least it needs , one that reads the schedule is a `dispatcher`, not an
`admin` , because every permission rule that applies to a person holding those
roles applies to the key.

Revoking is in the same place, and takes effect on the very next request.

**Key management is deliberately absent from the reference below**, and that is
not an oversight. `/apiKeys` is the one part of this API a key cannot use: a key
cannot create, list or revoke a key, even one holding the admin role. If it
could, a single leaked key would be a permanent foothold , you revoke it and
whatever took it has already issued itself three more. So those routes answer
403 to a key, and documenting them beside endpoints that work would be a trap.
Everything in the reference works with the credential this page tells you to use.

Everything after that , every request your software makes , uses the key:

```bash
export AERSCHEDULER_KEY=ask_live_…

curl -s https://api.aerscheduler.com/resources/aircraft \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $AERSCHEDULER_KEY"
```

That is the whole setup. There is no sign-in step and no token to refresh: a key
is a long-lived credential you store once, and it keeps working until you revoke
it or its expiry passes.

Keys carry **roles**, so a key is scoped to what it actually needs. A key that
reads the schedule should be a `dispatcher`, not an `admin`. Every permission
rule that applies to a person holding those roles applies to the key.

Creating and revoking keys requires a signed-in administrator , a key cannot mint
another key, so a leaked key cannot issue itself replacements.

## Conventions

Every one of these holds across the whole API, so you can write one client wrapper and stop thinking about it:

- **Responses are wrapped.** A body-bearing success is `{ "data": … }`. An error is `{ "message": "…" }`, and the message is written to be safe to show a user. A few endpoints noted individually break this: `/health`, the CSV export, and the OAuth redirects.
- **Status codes mean what they say.** `200` read or update, `201` created, `204` done with nothing to return, `400` your request was wrong, `401` sign in again, `403` signed in but not allowed, `404` no such thing, `429` slow down.
- **`401` and `403` are different.** `401` means the token is dead , get a new one. `403` means the token is fine and the answer is still no; retrying will not help.
- **Collections are `GET /thing`, items are `GET /thing/{id}`.** Create is `POST` to the collection, update is `PATCH` to the item, delete is `DELETE` on the item. Where a resource deviates, the endpoint says so.
- **Your organization is implied.** The token carries it. You never pass an organization id, and you can never read another organization's records.
- **Ids are integers** and stable for the life of the record.
- **Money is in cents**, as an integer. Never a float.

## Time zones

Scheduling is anchored to the **airport's** time zone, not the caller's device. A booking made at 7am at the field is 7am at the field regardless of where the person making it happens to be.

In practice that means: send `start` and `end` with an **explicit UTC offset or `Z`**. A bare local datetime like `2026-08-04T15:00:00` is rejected , it would be read in the server's zone and silently book a different instant than the person picked. Send `timeZoneName` (an IANA zone) alongside so the booking knows which zone it was made in.

## Reservation types

Which `type` a caller may create depends on the roles they hold. Roles are additive: an instructor who is also a technician may create both sets.

| Role | May create |
|---|---|
| owner, admin, dispatcher | solo, dual, ground, guest, sim, rental, maintenance |
| instructor | solo, dual, ground, guest, sim |
| student | solo, dual, ground, sim |
| renter | rental |
| technician | maintenance |

## Rate limits

Limits are applied per signed-in account, not per IP, so a whole school behind one office address does not share one budget.

| | Limit |
|---|---|
| Per account | 300 requests/minute, 5,000/hour |
| Unauthenticated | 100 requests per 5 minutes, per IP |
| Unauthenticated endpoints | Tighter still, and limited per IP |

Every response carries `RateLimit-Limit`, `RateLimit-Remaining`, and `RateLimit-Reset`. A `429` carries `Retry-After` in seconds , honour it rather than retrying on a fixed interval.

## Pagination

**Every list is capped at 1,000 rows**, whether or not you ask for a limit. Pass `limit` and `offset` to page:

```
GET /reservations?startDate=…&endDate=…&limit=100&offset=200
```

Every list response carries a `pagination` object beside `data`:

```json
{
  "data": [ … ],
  "pagination": { "total": 7823, "limit": 1000, "offset": 0, "returned": 1000, "hasMore": true }
}
```

- `total` , how many there are in all, before the page was taken.
- `returned` , how many are in `data` right now.
- `hasMore` , whether another page exists. **Check it.** It is how you find out a collection is bigger than one page, and some of ours are: our largest school has over 7,000 reservations.

Asking for more than 1,000 gives you 1,000 rather than an error, so you never need to know the ceiling to write a working request. `offset` past the end returns an empty `data` and `hasMore: false`.

Cursor pagination is coming and will be additive , `limit`/`offset` will keep working.

### Ordering

`sort` names a field to order by, as a dot path into the row, and `order` is `asc` (the default) or `desc`:

```
GET /invoices?sort=total&order=desc&limit=50
```

**Sort here rather than after you receive the page.** Ordering is applied to the whole collection before the page is cut, so `sort=total&order=desc&limit=50` gives you the fifty largest invoices. Sorting the page yourself orders the fifty rows you happen to be holding, which is a different , and usually wrong , answer.

Numbers order as numbers and ISO timestamps as instants, so `total` does not put `1000` before `90`. Empty values sort last in both directions: an invoice with no `paidAt` is not the most recent payment. Ties keep the endpoint's own order, so paging a sort by a coarse field like status will not skip or repeat rows.

Omit `sort` and you get the order the endpoint has always used.

## Versioning

**The unprefixed paths are v1.** `https://api.aerscheduler.com/reservations` is the v1 reservations endpoint; there is no `/v1/` to add and adding one will 404. That is deliberate , a version segment you never change is decoration, and we would rather not pretend.

This document describes **v1.0.0**, which you can read at `info.version` in the spec.

**What can change under you, without notice:**

- New endpoints.
- New fields on an existing response.
- New optional request parameters.
- New values in an enum you are already handling.

So parse leniently: ignore fields you do not recognise, and do not assume an enum is closed. An integration that breaks when we add a field is an integration that will break.

**What will never change within v1:**

- An endpoint disappearing, or moving.
- A field disappearing from a response, or changing type.
- A previously optional request parameter becoming required.
- A success status code changing.

Anything in that second list means **v2**, which would be served alongside v1 at `/v2/…` rather than replacing it. You would get notice by email before it existed, and v1 would keep working for a stated period afterwards , we are not going to break a customer's software to save ourselves a route table.

**Deprecations** are announced in the changelog and carry a `Deprecation` header on the affected endpoint before anything is removed.

tags.name: Training
tags.description: Courses, syllabi, enrollments and training records. A course is trained under Part 61 or Part 141; the shape is identical and only the enforcement differs. A **published syllabus version is immutable** , revising it makes a new version, and an enrollment stays pinned to the one it started under. A student's standing against each requirement is a **ledger**: entries are only ever appended, and a correction is a reversing entry rather than an edit, so hours flown are always traceable to the lesson that earned them.

tags.name: Memberships
tags.description: What a club or an FBO charges people for **belonging**, as opposed to for flying. A plan carries a one-time join fee, recurring dues, or both; a membership is one person's copy of a plan with the money **snapshotted at the moment it started**, so re-pricing a plan never re-prices anybody already on it. Every dues period is a ledger row, and a period is billed because the membership's own cursor says it is owed , never because of what day it happens to be. Dues and join fees are raised as ordinary invoices, so they appear under **Invoices** and in the revenue reports with everything else.

patch.description:
Retires somebody from the roster, or brings them back. Requires the **admin** role , a dispatcher cannot.

An archived member **is not notified, ever** , no email, no push, no in-app notice. They are left out of `GET /orgUsers` unless you pass `archived=true` (which is also how you list them again), and they cannot be added to a booking. Nothing is deleted: their flights, invoices and history are untouched, and restoring them is the same call with `false`.

Use this rather than grounding to tidy a roster. **Grounding is a live restriction and emails the member**, so grounding a batch of people who stopped flying years ago sends each of them an unexpected notice.

**Several people may share a side.** How many depends on the booking type: a `ground` class takes up to 12 students, `sim` up to 6, `dual` and `solo` up to 4, and `rental` up to 4 renters. `maintenance` takes nobody and `guest` takes one guest. Exceeding a limit is a 400 naming the side and the number allowed.

**Order matters.** The first person on a side is the leading payer: they are billed when the organization's rule for a charge is "one person pays", and they take the remainder cent of an uneven division.

Everyone listed must be free for the slot and must meet the currency and grounding rules , the booking is refused naming whoever does not, not silently trimmed.

post.description:
Generates the bill for a closed-out flight. Requires the **admin** role.

**Returns an ARRAY.** A booking shared between several people produces one invoice PER PAYER , a Stripe invoice bills exactly one customer, so splitting a booking's cost has to be several invoices rather than one invoice with shares underneath it. A booking with one payer returns an array of one.

How the cost divides is set per organization and per booking type , see the cost-splitting rules in the console. With no rules configured, one person is billed for the whole booking, which is how this endpoint has always behaved.

**Partial success is possible and is not an error.** If the payment processor accepts some invoices and rejects another, the ones that succeeded are real and are returned, with a `warnings` array naming who could not be billed. Call this endpoint again to bill only the payers who still have no invoice , it will not duplicate the ones already raised. A 400 means nothing was billed at all.

A share below the processor's 50-cent minimum is skipped rather than raised, and reported in `warnings`.

put.description:
Records each person's stake in the cost of a booking: their own meter readings when the charge is split by the time each person flew, their percentage when it is split by set shares, or a waiver for somebody who is on the booking but owes nothing (a safety pilot).

**Replaces the whole set.** Shares have to total 100% across everybody, so merging one person into an existing set is how a total quietly stops adding up. Send everybody every time.

Only people already on the booking may be given a stake. Refused once the booking has been invoiced , the invoices describe the hours and shares they were computed from, and rewriting those underneath them would leave the money disagreeing with its own record.

Whether the shares total 100%, and whether the individual meter readings add up to what the aircraft actually ran, is checked when the booking is INVOICED rather than here , so a half-finished close-out can still be saved.

bearerAuth.description:
An API key, sent as `Authorization: Bearer ask_live_…`.

Create one in the web console at **Settings → API keys**. The secret is shown once and stored only as a hash , if you lose it, revoke the key and create another.

A key is scoped to one organization and carries the roles you gave it , every permission rule that applies to a member holding those roles applies to the key. Grant the least it needs.

coordinates.description: Geocoded position, when the address could be resolved.

ApiKey.description: A credential that lets software act on your organization's behalf. The secret is never included, only a hash is stored.

id.description: Unique identifier, stable for the life of the record.

prefix.description: The displayable head of the key. Not a secret, and not enough to reconstruct one.

roles.description: What the key can do. These are real roles, every rule that applies to a member holding them applies to the key.

expiresAt.description: When it stops working. Null means no expiry.

revokedAt.description: When it was revoked. Null while live.

lastUsedAt.description: When it last authenticated a request, to the nearest minute. Null if never used, which is how you find keys to turn off.

createdBy.description: The administrator who minted it. Null if they have since left.

ApiKeyWithSecret.description: A newly created key. This is the ONLY response that ever contains the secret, store it now.

id.description: Unique identifier, stable for the life of the record.

prefix.description: The displayable head of the key.

secret.description: The key itself. Send it as `Authorization: Bearer <secret>`. We store only a hash, so if you lose this you must revoke the key and mint another.

Pagination.description: Where this page sits in the whole collection. Present on every list response.

total.description: How many there are in all, before this page was taken.

limit.description: Rows requested for this page. 1000 unless you asked for fewer.

offset.description: Rows skipped to reach this page.

hasMore.description: Whether another page exists. Check this, some collections are larger than one page.

Organization.description: A flight school, club, or FBO. Every other record belongs to exactly one.

id.description: Unique identifier, stable for the life of the record.

code.description: Six-character join code members use to request access.

showInDirectory.description: Whether the organization opts into the public directory.

plan.description: Which plan the organization is on: `standard` or `enterprise`. Enterprise is what makes this API available at all.

scheduledDeletionAt.description: When set, the school will be hard-deleted at this time. Null means no countdown is running. Owners schedule via DELETE /organizations; admins cancel via POST /organizations/cancelDeletion.

coordinates.description: Geocoded position, when the address could be resolved.

Location.description: A base of operations, a field, hangar, or classroom building.

id.description: Unique identifier, stable for the life of the record.

showInDirectory.description: Whether this location appears in the public directory.

timeZone.description: IANA time zone of the field, e.g. `America/Denver`. Scheduling is anchored to the AIRPORT's zone, not the caller's device, see the Time zones section.

coordinates.description: Geocoded position, when the address could be resolved.

Plane.description: Aircraft-specific detail on a resource whose type is an aircraft.

category.description: What the aircraft is. Together with `aircraftClass` this replaces the four-value `categoryClass`, which could not describe a helicopter.

aircraftClass.description: Class within the category. Null where the category has no class rating (a glider) or nobody has said. Only classes belonging to the category are accepted: a rotorcraft takes `helicopter` or `gyroplane`, and any other pairing is rejected.

seats.description: Occupants the airframe holds. Null means nobody has said.

meterMode.description: Which meters this airframe has. `none` (a glider, a balloon) means flights on it are NOT invoiced automatically: there is no meter reading to derive hours from, so the operator raises those invoices by hand. Ramp-out and ramp-in are unaffected.

rampedIn.description: True when the aircraft is on the ramp and available.

grounded.description: True when the aircraft is unavailable for booking.

fuelEngine2.description: Fuel on board, engine 2, for twins.

dryRate.description: Dry rate per hour, in cents.

wetRate.description: Wet rate per hour, in cents.

overnightMinimumTenths.description:
This aircraft's least billable time per night away, in TENTHS of an hour, applied as a floor on a booking that spans nights. `20` bills at least 2.0 hours a night.

`null` means inherit the organization's figure; `0` means exempt this aircraft entirely. The two are not interchangeable, an exempt aircraft must stay exempt when the school-wide figure changes.

Resource.description: Anything that can be booked: an aircraft, a simulator, or a room. The `type` object carries whichever detail applies.

id.description: Unique identifier, stable for the life of the record.

type.description: Exactly one of these is populated.

User.description: A person. One account can belong to many organizations.

id.description: Unique identifier, stable for the life of the record.

email.description: Email address. Unique across the system.

emailVerifiedAt.description: When the address was verified. Null means unverified.

UserDetails.description: A person's contact record. Returned only to the person themselves, an admin or dispatcher of your organization, or an instructor the person is assigned to as a student, so expect it to be absent on most reads.

phone.description: Primary, SMS-capable number, in **E.164** (`+13035551234`). Numbers sent to this API are normalized to E.164 on write and rejected if they are not real, dialable numbers; a number with no country code is read as US unless you send `defaultCountry`.

phoneCountry.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country of `phone`, so it can be re-rendered nationally.

dateOfBirth.description: Date of birth, `YYYY-MM-DD`. A calendar date, no time, no zone.

preferredName.description: What they go by, when that isn't their legal first name.

coordinates.description: Geocoded position, when the address could be resolved.

emergencyContacts.description: Everyone on this person's emergency list, primary first.

EmergencyContact.description: Who to call about a person in an emergency.

id.description: Unique identifier, stable for the life of the record.

relationship.description: How they are related. Free text.

altPhone.description: Second number to try, in E.164.

notes.description: Anything else worth knowing when calling.

isPrimary.description: True for the one to try first. At most one per person.

sortOrder.description: Display order within the person's list.

OrganizationUser.description: A person's membership of an organization. This (not `User`) is what schedules, invoices, and permissions hang off, because one person can belong to several organizations with different roles in each.

id.description: Unique identifier, stable for the life of the record.

roles.description: Roles held in this organization. Additive and non-hierarchical: a person can be both instructor and technician.

archivedAt.description: When the organization retired this person from its roster; null for a current member. Archived members receive no notifications of any kind, are omitted from member lists unless asked for, and cannot be booked. Distinct from `grounded`, which is a live restriction on somebody who is still here.

approvedForResource.description: Whether this member is checked out on the aircraft named by the request's `approvedForResourceId`. Present only when that filter was passed; absent otherwise.

Reservation.description: A booking of a resource, a person, or both.

id.description: Unique identifier, stable for the life of the record.

title.description: Short label shown on the calendar.

type.description: What kind of booking this is. Which types a caller may CREATE depends on their roles, see the Reservation types section.

start.description: Start instant. MUST carry an explicit offset or `Z`.

end.description:
End instant. MUST carry an explicit offset or `Z`.

MAY fall on a later calendar day than `start`. A school with multi-day bookings enabled can book a trip that keeps the resource for the whole span, and the resource is unavailable for every day in between rather than becoming free again each morning. Do not assume a booking ends on the day it starts.

timeZoneName.description: IANA zone the booking is anchored to, e.g. `America/Denver`. Resolved from the LOCATION, falling back to the organization, not from the caller's device, because how many nights a trip spans decides what it bills.

cancelledAt.description: When it was cancelled. Null for a live booking.

cancellationCategory.description: Fixed-list reason. Null on bookings cancelled before this was introduced, and on those the system cancelled for you, reports count those as “Not recorded”, not as a category somebody chose. May also read back a RETIRED value such as `other`, which is no longer accepted on write but is still reported on.

rrule.description: Recurrence rule, when this booking belongs to a repeating series.

invoices.description:
ONE PER PAYER. A booking shared between several people mints an invoice each, a Stripe invoice bills exactly one customer. A booking with one payer has an array of one, and an un-billed booking has an empty array.

Do not read `invoices[0]` as "the invoice": on a split booking that is one person's share. Ask whether EVERY payer has one.

invoice.description: **Deprecated, use `invoices`.** The first non-void invoice, kept so clients written before split billing keep working. On a booking with one payer this is exactly what it always meant; on a split booking it is only ONE person's share, so anything that reports whether a flight has been billed should read `invoices`. This field will be removed.

review.description: Close-out figures, populated once the flight is ramped out and back in.

id.description: Unique identifier, stable for the life of the record.

priority.description: How urgent it is. Set when the squawk is filed; `normal` if nothing was given.

grounding.description: Convenience for `priority == "grounding"`. Records the reporter's judgement that the aircraft should not fly. It does NOT set the aircraft's `grounded` flag, which is an administrator action on the resource itself.

resolvedAt.description: When it was cleared. Null while open.

MaintenanceDue.description: How much is left on a reminder, worked out from its template's interval and the aircraft's current meters. Computed on read, it is not stored.

kind.description: What the interval is counted in.

status.description: Which band it is in. `dueSoon` is the template's own warning period, the same threshold that sends the warning notification.

name.description: The template's name, lifted so a row can be rendered without it.

grounds.description: Whether coming due takes the aircraft off the line.

dueAt.description: When it comes due. Null on a meter-based interval, nobody can know the date.

daysRemaining.description: Whole days until `dueAt`. Negative means overdue.

basis.description: Which meter a meter-based interval counts.

dueAtHours.description: Meter reading it comes due at, in tenths of an hour.

hoursRemaining.description: Tenths of an hour left on that meter. Negative means overdue.

currentHours.description: What the meter reads now, in tenths of an hour.

progress.description: 0 is a fresh interval, 1 is due now, above 1 is overdue.

urgency.description: Sort key, ascending is most urgent first, comparable across all three kinds.

MaintenanceReminder.description: A due-date or due-hours reminder against one aircraft.

id.description: Unique identifier, stable for the life of the record.

startHours.description: Meter reading the interval started at.

completedAt.description: When the work was signed off.

MaintenanceReminderTemplate.description: The rule a maintenance reminder repeats on.

id.description: Unique identifier, stable for the life of the record.

repeat.description: Whether a new interval starts when this one is signed off.

ground.description: Whether the aircraft is grounded when this comes due.

remindDays.description: Interval in days, for date-based reminders.

remindDaysBefore.description: How many days ahead to warn.

remindHours.description: Interval in hours, for meter-based reminders.

remindHoursBefore.description: How many hours ahead to warn.

InspectionPreset.description: A ready-made inspection interval. Reference data: POST its `payload` to `/maintenance/reminders/templates` to actually create one.

id.description: Stable identifier for the preset.

letter.description: Which letter of the AVIATES mnemonic this covers. Null for the presets outside it.

interval.example: Every 100 hours on the tach, warn 10 hours out

caveat.description: Where the default does not apply to every aircraft.

ground.description: Whether the default grounds the aircraft when it comes due.

Invoice.description: A bill for a completed reservation. In ledger mode, member close-outs and desk charges may return an invoice-shaped stub instead of a Stripe invoice row.

id.description: Unique identifier, stable for the life of the record.

paidAt.description: When it was paid. Null while outstanding.

isLedgerCharge.description: True when this payload is a ledger charge stub (flight_charge / item_charge / fee), not a Stripe Invoice row. Clients must not call retrieveInvoice on these ids.

ledgerEntryId.description: Ledger entry id when `isLedgerCharge` is true. Same as `id` on the stub.

LedgerEntry.description: One append-only money movement on a member's account. Corrections are reversing entries, never edits. Partial top-up refunds link via `refundsTopupId`.

id.description: Unique identifier.

amountCents.description: Signed cents. Credits positive; charges negative.

type.description: topup | cash | check | other | adjustment | flight_charge | item_charge | fee | refund | reversal

createdBy.description: The member who posted this entry, when a person did (desk credit, refund, close-out).

invoiceId.description: Linked Stripe invoice when money moved through Stripe.

reversesId.description: Set on reversals: the entry this one reverses.

stripePaymentIntentId.description: Stripe PaymentIntent id on card top-ups.

stripeRefundId.description: Stripe Refund id when money returned to the card.

refundsTopupId.description: Top-up this refund draws down (partial refunds).

LedgerEntryItem.description: One line on a ledger entry.

id.description: Line id.

unitPrice.description: Unit price in cents (signed; qty × unitPrice rolls up to the entry amount).

MemberLedger.description: A member's account balance and recent ledger entries. Present whether or not the org has ledger mode enabled (balance is 0 with an empty list when unused).

balanceCents.description: Cached account balance in cents. Positive = credit; negative = amount owed.

ledgerEnabled.description: Whether this organization is in ledger billing mode.

LedgerStatement.description: Inclusive period statement for one member. Opening is the sum of entries strictly before `start`. Closing is opening plus the period sum.

closingCents.description: Balance at the end of the period.

entries.description: Oldest-first period entries, each with running balance.

LedgerStatementEntry.description: One statement line with running balance after the entry.

id.description: Ledger entry id.

amountCents.description: Signed cents. Credits positive; charges negative.

runningBalanceCents.description: Balance after this entry, starting from the period opening.

LedgerReceipt.description: Printable receipt for a ledger charge (flight / item / fee). Replaces Stripe PDF when the org is in ledger mode.

id.description: Organization id.

reservation.description: Linked booking when this is a flight charge.

id.description: Reservation id.

LedgerAccount.description: One member on the school-wide ledger roster. Positive balanceCents is credit on account; negative is amount owed.

balanceCents.description: Cached account balance in cents. Positive = credit; negative = amount owed.

lastActivityAt.description: When the latest ledger entry was posted.

owingSince.description: When the running balance last crossed into negative and has stayed there. Null when they do not owe.

daysOwing.description: Whole days from owingSince to now. Null when they do not owe.

LedgerAccountSummary.description: Org-wide ledger totals for the current (non-archived) roster. Not scoped to the list filter.

receivableCents.description: Sum of amounts owed (absolute value of negative balances).

OrganizationLedgerSettings.description: Org-wide ledger billing mode and optional card surcharge on member top-ups. Independent of Stripe Connect billing settings. Default off / no surcharge.

enabled.description: When true, members use an account balance (top-ups, desk credit, refunds). Member flight and custom charges post to the ledger.

topUpCardFeePercent.description: Card surcharge on top-ups, hundredths of a percent (290 = 2.9%). Null or 0 = no percent. Does not apply to desk cash/check credit. Same units as invoice serviceFeePercent.

topUpCardFeeFlatCents.description: Flat cents added on each card top-up (30 = $0.30). Null or 0 = none. Stacks with the percent.

lateFeePercent.description: Whole percent of the amount owing (5 = 5%). Null or 0 = no percent. Ledger mode only.

lateFeeFlatCents.description: Flat cents added on each monthly late-fee post. Null or 0 = none.

lateFeeGraceDays.description: Days a balance may stay negative before a late fee posts. Null = 30 when a percent or flat is set. 0 = fee on the first eligible sweep after they go owing.

LedgerAutoRefill.description: Per-member auto-refill (ledger Auto Pay). Charges the default saved card on a cadence. Ledger mode only.

enabled.description: When true, the hourly cron may charge this member.

mode.description: under_threshold (balance < threshold, charge chargeCents), pay_balance (charge abs owing), or fixed_amount (charge chargeCents even at zero).

thresholdCents.description: under_threshold: fire when balance is below this. 0 = fire once owing.

chargeCents.description: under_threshold and fixed_amount: ledger credit to charge (before card surcharge). Minimum 100.

runHourLocal.description: Hour 0–23 in the organization time zone. First attempt waits until this hour. Default 4.

lastSuccessAt.description: Last successful charge. Used for period idempotency.

consecutiveFailures.description: Failed attempts in the current period.

pausedReason.description: Why enabled is false after a pause.

LedgerTopUpIntent.description: Client secrets for a ledger card top-up PaymentIntent on the org's connected Stripe account.

clientSecret.description: PaymentIntent client secret for Stripe.js / Payment Element.

orgStripeAccountId.description: Connected account the Intent lives on.

customerId.description: Stripe customer id on that connected account.

ephemeralKey.description: Ephemeral key for native Payment Sheet. Null when already confirmed.

confirmed.description: True when the server confirmed with a saved paymentMethodId.

creditCents.description: Amount credited to the member ledger.

feeCents.description: Org card surcharge included in the charge (0 when none).

chargeCents.description: Total charged to the card = creditCents + feeCents.

balanceCents.description: Current ledger balance after a saved-card confirm. Omitted when the Intent still needs Stripe.js.

LedgerTopUpConfirm.description: Ledger balance after Stripe.js confirmed a card top-up PaymentIntent.

credited.description: True when this call posted the credit. False when it was already posted.

LedgerRefundableTopup.description: A card top-up that still has refundable remainder for the desk Refund UI.

id.description: Ledger entry id of the top-up.

stripePaymentIntentId.description: PaymentIntent to refund via Stripe when present.

LedgerRefundable.description: Balance plus refundable top-ups for the desk Refund flow.

topups.description: Newest-first card top-ups with remaining refundable cents.

MembershipPlan.description: What an organization charges people to belong, a one-time join fee, recurring dues, or both. Tiers are plans: full, associate, social.

id.description: Unique identifier, stable for the life of the record.

archivedAt.description: When the plan was retired. Retired plans stop being offered to new members; everyone already on one keeps being billed.

joinFeeCents.description: One-time fee to join, in cents. Null when there is none.

joinFeeLabel.description: How the join fee reads on the invoice.

duesCents.description: Recurring dues, in cents. Null for a plan with no ongoing cost.

duesLabel.description: How the dues read on the invoice.

duesDayOfMonth.description: The day every member on this plan is billed, 1-28. Null bills each member on their own join anniversary instead.

prorateFirstPeriod.description: Whether somebody joining mid-cycle is charged a part-period for the days they actually get.

autoBillDues.description: Whether each period's invoice is raised automatically, overnight.

duesDueInDays.description: Days to pay a dues or joining-fee invoice. Null means no due date.

bookingWindowDays.description: How far ahead a member on this tier may book. Null means no limit.

memberCount.description: How many live memberships are on this plan. Not its history.

MembershipPlanRate.description: What one tier pays per hour for one aircraft, overriding the aircraft's published rate. Sparse: only the aircraft a plan disagrees with have a row.

id.description: Unique identifier, stable for the life of the record.

wetRate.description: Cents per hour, wet. Wins over dry, matching ordinary pricing.

Membership.description: One person's membership of one organization. The money is a **snapshot** taken when it started, so re-pricing the plan never re-prices this member.

id.description: Unique identifier, stable for the life of the record.

status.description: `pending`, set up, not started, bills nothing. `active`, the only status that accrues dues. `suspended`, paused, keeps the row and stops the meter. `cancelled`, over, and terminal.

joinFeeCents.description: The join fee as it stood on the day this member joined, in cents.

duesCents.description: Dues as they stood on the day this member joined, in cents.

nextDueAt.description: The start of the next period that has not been charged. **The billing cursor**: a period is owed because this says so, never because of what day it is. Null on a membership that is not accruing dues.

autoBillDues.description: Whether this member's periods are invoiced automatically.

agreementOnFileAt.description: When staff recorded that the member's agreement is on file. A record only, nothing is gated on it.

charges.description: Recent dues periods. Present on a single-membership read.

MembershipCharge.description: One dues period, and what happened to it. The period is half-open: `periodEnd` is the first day NOT covered.

periodEnd.description: Day after the last day of the period.

amountCents.description: What was charged, in cents. A prorated part-period differs from the membership's dues.

status.description: `pending`, owed, not yet invoiced. `billed`, an invoice exists. `waived`, deliberately not charged. `failed`, billing was attempted and refused, and the row is kept so it can be retried.

note.description: Why, when it is not a plain charge.

id.description: Unique identifier, stable for the life of the record.

expireAt.description: When it stops being shown. Expired notices are swept hourly.

forRoles.description: Roles that should see it. Empty means everyone.

seenAt.description: When the signed-in member marked this notice as seen (Got it). Null if they have not. Seen notices leave Home and stay on the announcements page.

Notification.description: An in-app notification for one member.

id.description: Unique identifier, stable for the life of the record.

link.description: Deep link into the app or console.

readAt.description: When it was read. Null while unread.

CurrencyType.description: A recurring requirement members must stay current on, a flight review, a medical, a checkout.

id.description: Unique identifier, stable for the life of the record.

expiresOn.description: A fixed expiry date, for one-off requirements.

warningPeriodInDays.description: How long before expiry to start warning.

canRenewSelf.description: Whether a member may sign off their own renewal.

instructorCanRenew.description: Whether an instructor may sign it off.

dispatcherCanRenew.description: Whether a dispatcher may sign it off.

Currency.description: One member's standing against one currency type. Created automatically when a type is attached to a member group, there is no endpoint that creates one directly.

id.description: Unique identifier, stable for the life of the record.

DocumentType.description: A category of member document, medical, photo ID, endorsement.

id.description: Unique identifier, stable for the life of the record.

restricted.description: When true, only administrators may upload documents of this type on a member's behalf.

UserDocument.description: A file held against a member.

id.description: Unique identifier, stable for the life of the record.

url.description: Location of the file. Fetch through the signed-URL endpoint rather than linking directly.

Group.description: A named set of members or resources, used to scope requirements and permissions in bulk.

id.description: Unique identifier, stable for the life of the record.

Availability.description: A window in which a person or resource is free.

id.description: Stable identifier to pass to `POST /reports/run`.

ReportResult.description: The output of a report run.

unit.description: Unit, where the value is not a plain number.

rows.description: Result rows, keyed by column key.

totals.description: Column totals, where the column is summable.

SearchResult.description: One match, flattened to a common shape.

type.description: Which kind of record this is.

id.description: The record's id, within its own type.

subtitle.description: Context under the title, who, what, or where.

date.description: The date this record turns on, unformatted. See `dateLabel`.

timeZone.description: IANA zone `date` belongs to. Null means the reader's own.

params.description: Ids needed to open this record, keyed by name.

SearchResults.description: Matches across every entity type the caller may see.

q.description: The query that was run. Empty when browsing.

types.description: Every type this caller may search, the full category list, not just the types that matched. Narrowed by role: a member who cannot read squawks never sees `squawk` here.

results.description: The matches, grouped by type in the order of `types`.

AuditEvent.description: One recorded thing somebody did. Append-only: audit events are never edited or deleted.

action.description: Dotted and past tense: `reservation.rescheduled`, `invoice.voided`, `resource.grounded`. Stable: values are never renamed, because rows written months ago still carry the old string.

entityType.description: What kind of thing it happened to.

entityId.description: The id of that thing. Not a foreign key, an event outlives the row it describes, so this can point at something that has since been deleted.

summary.description: A finished sentence, written when the event was recorded.

changes.description: Only the fields that moved, as `{ field: { from, to } }`.

source.description: `web`, `ios`, `api`, or `system`. Null when it could not be determined.

actor.description: Who did it. Null for system-originated events.

subject.description: The member the event is about, which is usually not the actor.

resource.description: The aircraft, simulator or room it touched, if any.

StandbyInterest.description: A member's request to be considered when a matching scheduling slot opens.

id.description: Unique identifier, stable for the life of the record.

kind.description: How this interest matches: one reservation, a time window, or standing criteria.

expiresAt.description: When this interest stops matching, if set.

reservationType.description: Optional reservation type filter on the interest row.

criteria.description: Standing match criteria. Empty lists mean any. Used when kind is standing.

watchedReservation.description: Reservation watched when kind is on_reservation.

resource.description: Optional resource filter on the interest row.

instructorOrgUser.description: Optional instructor filter on the interest row.

notificationDelivery.description: Channels currently enabled for slot offers.

anyChannelEnabled.description: At least one delivery channel is enabled.

SlotOffer.description: A time-limited offer to claim an available scheduling slot.

id.description: Unique identifier, stable for the life of the record.

trigger.description: How the offer began: cancel_recovery from a canceled booking, desk from staff, system from AerScheduler AI idle-window scanner.

purpose.description: claim books the seat; instructor_confirm asks the instructor to confirm first.

timeZoneName.description: IANA time zone used to present the slot.

respondedAt.description: When the offer left pending state.

offerGroupId.description: Stable id shared by each candidate in one recovery chain.

offeredTo.description: Member who may accept this offer.

createdBy.description: Desk member who created a desk offer, if any.

standbyInterest.description: Interest that matched this offer, if any.

notificationDelivery.description: Channels currently enabled for slot offers for the recipient.

anyChannelEnabled.description: At least one delivery channel is enabled.

Error.description: Every error response has this shape.

message.description: Human-readable explanation, safe to show a user.

retryAfter.description: Seconds to wait before retrying. Present on 429 only.
